name: Slint
label: Touch and Go
lede: Slint took its name from a pet fish, split up months before its second album came out, and never toured it. Spiderland has sold year after year since, to people who swear it changed how a rock band can sound.

eras.title: Named after a pet fish
eras.text: Britt Walford and Brian McMahan had played together since middle school at Louisville's Brown School, then in Squirrel Bait. Walford and David Pajo came out of the prog-punk band Maurice, whose last songs became Slint's first. They wanted a heavier, stranger band, and Big Black and the Minutemen showed them how.

years.h: Walford and McMahan go from Languid and Flaccid to Squirrel Bait
years.p: The two start playing together in middle school with [[Ned Oldham|57b40135-dad3-4514-9e28-fc446cf20585]] as Languid and Flaccid, then land in [[Squirrel Bait|5dbf117b-c076-4d3b-b7ae-13517c25b2cf]]. Walford's other band with David Pajo, Maurice, fades out as they chase a [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]]-style sound.

years.h: Most of a Unitarian congregation walks out two songs in
years.p: Britt Walford, David Pajo and 18-year-old bassist Ethan Buckler play their first show, on November 2, as Small Tight Dirty Tufts of Hair. The audience is a Unitarian Universalist congregation.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the congregation left during the first two songs.

years.h: McMahan joins on guitar, and a pet fish names the band
years.p: Brian McMahan comes in and the band renames itself Slint, after one of Walford's pet fish.

years.h: Walford asks Albini for a bass drum like a ham in a catcher's mitt
years.p: Slint picks [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] to record Tweez because of [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]]. At the mixdown Walford asks for that ham sound, then spills a cup of tea on Albini's mixing board.
years.xp: Most of the words were made up in the studio; the band left in ad-libbed talk and sound effects between songs. Eight of the nine tracks are named after band members' parents, and the ninth, Rhoda, after Walford's dog.

years.h: Bassist Ethan Buckler quits and starts King Kong
years.p: Unhappy with the Tweez sessions, Buckler leaves and forms [[King Kong|fd95f811-981e-4802-a712-f023fc4197fb]], which at first has all the Slint members on different instruments.

eras.title: The record a friend paid for
eras.text: Touch and Go didn't answer, so a friend put up the money for Tweez. By the time it came out, most of Slint was in college, coming home on breaks to rehearse in the Walfords' basement, repeating riffs until they changed shape.

years.h: Todd Brashear takes over the bass, and keeps it through Spiderland
years.p: Brashear steps in for Buckler in 1988 and stays until the end.

yt: Slint soundcheck, "Breadcrumb Trail," Court Tavern, Aug 25 1989
years.h: Tweez comes out on a label that exists for one record
years.p: Touch and Go didn't respond, so Slint's friend Jennifer Hartman paid for a tiny pressing. Tweez is the only release on Jennifer Hartman Records.

eras.title: Four days, then nothing
eras.text: Slint wrote Spiderland slowly and recorded it fast with Brian Paulson, then stopped being a band before it came out. No tour, no interviews, no photo shoot, no video. Brian McMahan had nearly died in a car crash that year, and the record carries it.

years.h: Walford drums on The Breeders' Pod as Shannon Doughton
years.p: Slint's drummer plays on [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]]' debut, recorded by [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], under a made-up name. On the Safari EP he's Mike Hunt.

years.h: McMahan's car crash on the way to a Bastro session
years.p: Driving to watch Brian Paulson record [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]], McMahan is in a near-fatal crash. A paramedic calls it in as Code 138, and McMahan comes to singing the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]]' We Are 138.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the crash deeply affected McMahan and shaped the Spiderland sessions. He had worked out his vocals at home on a four-track, sitting in his parents' car to get the quiet spoken parts to sit under loud instruments.

years.big: I did not want to rehearse the vocals
years.h: Spiderland goes down in four days at River North
years.p: Brian Paulson records Slint live in Chicago in August. McMahan, per Wikipedia, wanted his vocals as a one-shot. Two takes or fewer, one mic for the whispers and one for the screams.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says McMahan and Walford wrote the words at the last minute, in the studio, with the vocal melodies worked out ahead of time.

McMahan's own description of the vocals, as Wikipedia prints it: "a one-shot, cathartic experience." No effects went into the mix.

years.h: Will Oldham shoots the cover in an Indiana quarry lake
years.p: A longtime friend, [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]], photographs the band treading water in an abandoned quarry in Utica, Indiana. The cover is just four heads above the surface.

years.h: Slint is over by November, months before Spiderland ships
years.p: No tour, no interviews, no band. According to Wikipedia, the story told since is that McMahan checked into a hospital right after the sessions and was treated for depression.

years.h: Spiderland lands on Touch and Go and sells a few thousand in year one
years.p: Six songs, from Breadcrumb Trail to Good Morning, Captain, which is Pajo's favorite. An ad on the sleeve invites female vocalists to write to a Louisville address; [[PJ Harvey|e795e03d-b5d5-4a5f-834d-162cfb308a2c]] was among those who answered.
years.xp:
Don, Aman is a deliberate anagram of Madonna, Nosferatu Man takes off from the 1922 film, and the instrumental For Dinner... uses no pedals at all.

Wikipedia puts first-year sales at only a few thousand copies, and says that years later it was still under 5,000. The same article lists Metacritic at 99 and Pitchfork's 2014 remaster at 10 out of 10.

years.big: In 10 years it will be a landmark
years.h: Albini gives Spiderland "ten fucking stars" in Melody Maker
years.p: Steve Albini, who recorded Tweez, reviews the record for Melody Maker and tells readers to buy it now, before they have to scramble for a copy.
years.xp: Wikipedia prints the rest of the line: "you'll have to scramble to buy a copy then." NME gave the album 7/10 in 1991.

eras.title: Everybody else's band
eras.text: Slint didn't exist, but Spiderland kept selling several thousand copies a year, according to Breadcrumb Trail, which is a lot for an indie record by a dead band. Its whisper-to-scream shape turned into a genre, and the members turned up all over it.

years.h: Touch and Go puts Tweez back in print
years.p: The label reissues the debut in 1993, two years after Spiderland and three after the band stopped.

years.h: Two Albini tracks from 1989 finally come out as an untitled 10-inch
years.p: Slint cut two instrumentals with Steve Albini for a 12-inch on Jennifer Hartman Records, then shelved them when Touch and Go's [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] got interested. Five years later: Glenn and a new Rhoda.

years.h: McMahan starts the For Carnation while Pajo joins Tortoise
years.p: [[The For Carnation|f3b9bb88-e82a-44e0-9f81-ae3acd4f8436]] is McMahan's. Pajo goes on to [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]], [[Palace|44d766e3-fc4a-4c19-9cdc-cd69966de1d8]], [[Papa M|6edbe0fb-734e-4b1d-9c64-73ebb04853e1]], [[Zwan|5af2629b-36de-486c-ad50-a89a28ff050f]] and [[Interpol|b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e]]; Walford plays in Evergreen.

eras.title: Playing it back
eras.text: Nearly fifteen years on, Slint came back on its own terms: short runs, no new album, Spiderland played front to back. A box set and a documentary closed the book, and the band stopped again.

years.cap: Slint on stage during the reunion shows, 2007
years.h: Slint plays its first shows in 15 years, after curating ATP
years.p: McMahan, Pajo and Walford curate All Tomorrow's Parties at Camber Sands, England, then play an 18-date tour and insist it's a one-time thing.

years.cap: Slint at the Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago, July 13, 2007
years.h: Slint plays Spiderland front to back and unveils King's Approach
years.p: Primavera Sound, ATP's Don't Look Back and Chicago's Pitchfork festival all get the full album. The new song, King's Approach, has never been recorded.
years.xp: Wikipedia's list of 2007 dates also has Barcelona, London, Seattle and Hollywood.

years.h: Todd Brashear runs Louisville's Wild and Woolly Video
years.p: The former bassist owns a Louisville rental store that outlasted almost every other.

years.h: Slint headlines the last ATP weekend at Camber Sands
years.p: The band returns to Camber Sands, where it curated in 2005, for the final All Tomorrow's Parties weekender there.

years.h: The Spiderland box set arrives with Lance Bangs' 90-minute film
years.p: Touch and Go's remaster adds 1989-90 live, demo and practice tapes, plus Breadcrumb Trail, which Bangs shot over 12 years. Metacritic scores it 99.

years.h: Slint finishes Primavera and Green Man, then stops again
years.p: Dates in Spain, Portugal and Wales end 2014 with no plans for new material.

years.h: David Pajo survives a suicide attempt
years.p: David Pajo attempts suicide after posting a long note on his blog, Wikipedia reports. He survives, and was reported to be recovering.

sources.title: Louisville Public Media: Off the Record, Todd Brashear
